title: From OBS to RACI
blurb: Use the organisational breakdown structure and the WBS to build a RACI with exactly one Accountable per work package.
question: Riverside Hospital is installing a new outpatient booking system with an external supplier. Staff keep asking who signs off testing and who should be asked about data. How does the project manager use the organisational breakdown structure to build a responsibility assignment matrix that settles this?

teach.body: The ORGANISATIONAL BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE (OBS) is a hierarchy showing the organisations, teams and roles involved in the project, including suppliers: it answers WHO. The WBS breaks the scope into work packages: it answers WHAT. Put the WBS down the side and the OBS across the top and you have a RESPONSIBILITY ASSIGNMENT MATRIX (RAM). RACI is the most common form: each cell says whether a role is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted or Informed for that work package.

teach.caption: The OBS shows the people and organisations doing the work, internal and external. It is not the company's whole org chart, just the project's slice of it.

letters.sub: Does the work. Can be one or more roles.
Owns the outcome and signs it off. Exactly one.
Gives input before or during the work: two-way.
Kept up to date afterwards: one-way.

Outpatients mgr

teach.caption: Read ACROSS a row: exactly one A. Read DOWN a column: a role with many Rs at the same time may be over-allocated. One role can hold A and R together.

rows.label: Role

teach.body: One A gives every work package a single owner who makes the decisions, answers for the result and signs it off. Two As means each assumes the other will act, or they contradict each other; no A means nobody owns it at all. Both lead to gaps, duplicated effort, delays and blame. The RACI also clarifies communication (who to consult, who to tell), speeds up onboarding, and feeds stakeholder engagement and resource planning.

In a LINEAR life cycle the RACI is built during definition from the full WBS and OBS, approved as part of the project management plan and kept under change control. In an ITERATIVE life cycle a self-organising team shares out tasks within each time box, so a detailed task-level RACI adds little. It is used at a higher level instead: the product owner accountable for backlog priorities, the team responsible for delivery, users consulted at each review.

teach.text: Exam traps: mixing up Responsible (does the work) with Accountable (owns and signs off); giving a work package two As 'for shared ownership'; and saying a RAM is built from the PBS or CBS. It is the OBS (who) crossed with the WBS (what).

teach.h: How this comes up in a written answer
items: Define the OBS: the hierarchy of organisations, teams and roles doing the project work.
Explain that crossing the OBS with the WBS work packages creates the RAM.
Explain RACI: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed, with one A per work package.
Give the benefit: clear ownership, no gaps or overlaps, clear communication lines.
Mention checks: one A per row, Rs not overloaded down a column, agreed with those named.
OBS = who (organisations, teams, roles, suppliers); WBS = what (work packages).
OBS × WBS = responsibility assignment matrix; RACI is its common form.
Responsible does the work; Accountable owns the result and signs off.
Exactly one A per work package; Rs can be several; one role can be A and R.
Consulted is two-way input before; Informed is one-way update after.

summary: You can now explain how the OBS (who) and the WBS (what) combine into a responsibility assignment matrix, and read or build a RACI. You can also explain why each work package needs exactly one Accountable role and how to check a RACI for gaps and overload.

A.q: A responsibility assignment matrix is created by combining which two structures?
A.why: The OBS (who) is crossed with the WBS (what): work packages on one axis, roles and teams on the other.

whyNot.0: The PBS lists products and the CBS lists costs; neither identifies who does the work.
whyNot.1: The CBS maps costs to the WBS; it does not assign responsibilities to people.
whyNot.3: The OBS is right, but responsibilities are assigned to work packages in the WBS, not to products.

A.q: In a RACI chart, what does 'C' stand for?
options: Confirmed: told once work is done
A.why: Consulted roles are asked for their input before or during the work: a two-way conversation.

whyNot.0: Signing off is the Accountable role.
whyNot.2: Suppliers can hold any letter; 'Contracted' is not part of RACI.
whyNot.3: Being told after the event is Informed, the one-way 'I'.

A.q: What does an organisational breakdown structure (OBS) show?
options: The work packages the scope needs
The products the project will deliver
The costs allocated to each package
The teams and roles doing the work
A.why: The OBS is a hierarchy of the organisations, teams and roles involved in the project, including external suppliers.

whyNot.0: Work packages are shown on the WBS.
whyNot.1: Products are shown on the PBS.
whyNot.2: Costs are shown on the CBS.

B.q: Riverside Hospital's RACI shows both the IT lead and the Outpatients manager as 'A' for user acceptance testing. What should the project manager do?
options: Leave it, as shared ownership helps
Mark both as 'R' and remove the A
Ask the sponsor to sign every test
B.why: Each work package needs exactly one Accountable role, so the PM should agree who owns UAT; the other can be Consulted or Responsible.

whyNot.1: Two As blurs ownership: each may wait for the other, or they may give conflicting decisions.
whyNot.2: Removing the A leaves nobody owning the result or signing it off.
whyNot.3: Pulling every test sign-off up to the sponsor overloads them and still leaves UAT without a clear owner.

B.q: Which statement best distinguishes Responsible from Accountable?
options: R signs off; A carries out the task
R is one person; A can be several
R is internal; A is the supplier
R does the work; A owns the result
B.why: The Responsible role carries out the work; the single Accountable role owns the outcome and signs it off.

whyNot.0: This is the wrong way round: A signs off and R does the work.
whyNot.1: Also reversed: there can be several Rs but only one A.
whyNot.2: Either letter can sit with an internal or external role.

B.q: Reading down one team member's column in a RACI shows twelve 'R' entries in the same month. What does this most likely reveal?
options: The WBS is missing work packages
That person must be the sponsor
The OBS has too many levels in it
B.why: Columns show each role's load. Many Rs at once is a warning to check the resource histogram for over-allocation.

whyNot.0: Many entries suggests a lot of work assigned, not missing work.
whyNot.2: Sponsors are usually Accountable or Informed at a high level, not Responsible for many packages.
whyNot.3: The number of OBS levels does not explain one person carrying so many Rs.

C.q:
Which TWO problems is a well-built RACI designed to prevent?
1) Work that nobody owns
2) Activities that have no float
3) Two people each assuming the other will act
4) Estimates that are too optimistic
C.why: A single A per package removes ownerless work (1) and the 'I thought you were doing it' gap (3).

whyNot.0: Float is a scheduling property; a RACI does not change it.
whyNot.1: Optimistic estimates are tackled by estimating methods and re-estimating, not by a RACI.
whyNot.2: Item 3 is right, but float (2) is about the schedule, not responsibilities.

C.q: An agile team delivers a new app in two-week time boxes. What is the most appropriate way to use a RACI?
options: Assign an 'A' to every daily task
Make the PM 'A' for every item
Use it at release and backlog level
Drop it, as agile teams have no roles
C.why: The team self-organises tasks within each time box, so the RACI is kept at a higher level: for example, the product owner accountable for backlog priorities and users consulted at reviews.

whyNot.0: Task-level As in a self-organising team add bureaucracy and cut across how the team shares work.
whyNot.1: The product owner, not the PM, is accountable for backlog priorities in iterative working.
whyNot.3: Agile has clear roles (product owner, team, users); clarity of accountability still matters.

C.q: The finance team are marked 'I' for the design of budget tracking. They complain they are only told after decisions that affect their systems. Which change best fixes this?
C.why: Consulted means giving input before decisions are made: exactly what finance needs.

whyNot.1: Finance want a say, not ownership; making them A would also challenge the existing owner.
whyNot.2: Removing them means they would not even be told.
whyNot.3: Responsible means doing the design work, which is not what they asked for.

reteach.title: Running the school summer fair
reteach.question: The parents' association is running the summer fair. Last year nobody knew who was in charge of the raffle and two people ordered the bouncy castle. How would a RACI fix that?

blocks.h: List the jobs, list the people, cross them
blocks.body: The jobs (cake stall, raffle, first aid) are the WBS. The people and groups (the chair, parent volunteers, the school office, the hire company) are the OBS. Cross them in a grid and give each job exactly one person who owns it: that stops the double-booked bouncy castle. Everyone else is marked as doing the work, being asked first, or just being told.

head: Job
Chair
Volunteers
School office
blocks.caption: One A in every row. The volunteers' column shows how much they are being asked to do.

blocks.text: The person who DOES the job (Responsible) is not always the one who ANSWERS for it (Accountable). The office books the castle; the chair owns the decision.

explain.body: A hierarchy of the organisations, departments, teams and roles involved in delivering the project, including suppliers and contractors. It shows reporting lines for the project, not the whole company.

test.q: Should an external supplier's staff appear in a project's OBS?
options: Yes, if they do project work
Only if they sit on the board
test.why: The OBS shows everyone organised to deliver the work, internal or external.

whyNot.0: Leaving suppliers out hides who does part of the work, so it cannot be assigned in the RAM.
whyNot.1: Once a contract ends they are no longer doing project work.
whyNot.3: Board membership is about governance; the OBS covers everyone delivering work.

explain.body: Work packages from the WBS form the rows; roles from the OBS form the columns. Each cell records that role's responsibility for that package. The result is the responsibility assignment matrix (RAM).

test.q: In a RAM, what normally forms the rows and the columns?
test.why: Work packages (from the WBS) and roles (from the OBS) form the two axes.

whyNot.1: Risk owners are recorded in the risk register.
whyNot.2: Costs per item belong to the CBS and budget.
whyNot.3: Activities against dates is a schedule or Gantt chart.

explain.body: Responsible: does the work. Accountable: owns the result, makes the decisions, signs off. Consulted: asked for input before or during (two-way). Informed: told about progress or decisions afterwards (one-way).

test.q: A user representative is sent the weekly progress update on training but is not asked for any input. Which RACI letter fits?
test.why: Receiving updates without being asked for input is one-way communication: Informed.

whyNot.0: They are not doing the training work.
whyNot.1: They do not own or sign off the training.
whyNot.2: Consulted would mean being asked for input.

explain.body: Every work package gets exactly one Accountable role. Then check across each row (one A, at least one R) and down each column (is anyone carrying too many Rs at once?). Agree the matrix with the people named before it is baselined.

rows.label: Row with one A and two Rs
Column with many Rs at once

test.q: Which check should be made on EVERY row of a finished RACI?
test.why: Each work package must have one, and only one, Accountable role.

whyNot.0: There can be any number of Consulted roles, including none.
whyNot.2: Informed entries are normal and often needed.
whyNot.3: Two As splits ownership; there must be exactly one.
